title: Line Breaker (working title) - Cozy Mobile Turn Based Brick Puzzle Game
author: w1a1s1p
selftext:
This is my first attempt at game dev. Let alone AI game dev.

I even cut a super simple trailer to show the game, some future enemies, and the overall vibe.

**The idea:** a jump-in, jump-out cozy puzzle game.    

* No energy bars.  
* No interstitial ads.  
* No banner ads.  
* No timers.  
* No rush.   

Each level plays like a little chess puzzle, with a bit of RNG to keep you honest.

**Inspiration:** 1010, Tetris, Block Puzzle, Puzzle Quest, Into the Breach, Slay the Spire.

**The toolbox:**

* Astra (Low and Medium) for most of the dev work with agentic work
* Jev from Typesafe for building, playtesting, and balancing levels, enemies, and abilities
* Blender MCP
* DaVinci Resolve MCP
* Local H3 Minimax for the background animation and music and sound effects
* GPT ImageGen 2.5 for concept art
* Tencent's Hunyuan 3D for image-to-3D (30 daily credits get you surprisingly far)

**Where I'm at:** almost one week in, one Codex reset burned, and I've already exported my first APK and played it on my own phone. 

The experience was just... wow. (Yes, I'm biased)

**My honest take:** AI game dev is absolutely possible. 

Rewind a year or two, and getting these results would have taken much more time, many more people, and much more money.

**Who am I?** Not a developer. Not a designer. Not an animator. 

My day job is online marketing and advertising. I just love turn-based games (X-Com, Jagged Alliance) and old-school Tetris and Lumines. 

And as a guy in his 40s with a family and responsibilities, most mobile games feel like cash grabs, or they bury you in so many ads it's unbearable. 

I just wanted something I'd personally enjoy.

Then my 8-year-old (my playtester) picked it up, and the first thing he said was: "Dad! I love these types of games. Did you make it?" followed by him finishing the first 10 levels and saying, "Is there more? When are you going to make more levels? Can I have it on my tablet?"

That was the boost. 

I'm taking this to the finish line and publishing on the Play Store. 

Even if it never makes a cent, I'll have a game I love playing.

Feedback is welcome, and I'm happy to answer any questions as best I can.
